entries.question: For every unordered pair of distinct transacted products sharing a customer, compute customer-set Jaccard similarity. Return columns: product_a, product_b, shared_customers, union_customers, jaccard. Order: product_a, product_b ascending. Use distinct non-NULL CustomerID/ProductID edges, product_a < product_b; union is customers buying either product, intersection is customers buying both.
entries.sql:
WITH t AS (
SELECT tr.*, CAST(Price AS DECIMAL(38,6)) AS p,
CASE WHEN Date IS NOT NULL AND Time REGEXP '^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]$'
THEN TIMESTAMP(Date,Time) ELSE NULL END AS ts FROM birdbench.transactions_1k tr),
m AS (SELECT CustomerID, Date AS ym, STR_TO_DATE(CONCAT(Date,'01'),'%Y%m%d') AS md,
CAST(Consumption AS DECIMAL(38,6)) AS v FROM birdbench.yearmonth
WHERE Date REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$' AND LEFT(Date,4) BETWEEN '1000' AND '9999')
, edges AS (SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID,ProductID FROM t WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND ProductID IS NOT NULL),
sizes AS (SELECT ProductID,COUNT(*) n FROM edges GROUP BY ProductID),
pairs AS (SELECT a.ProductID pa,b.ProductID pb,COUNT(*) n FROM edges a JOIN edges b ON a.CustomerID=b.CustomerID AND a.ProductID<b.ProductID GROUP BY a.ProductID,b.ProductID)
SELECT pa product_a,pb product_b,x.n shared_customers,a.n+b.n-x.n union_customers,ROUND(CAST(x.n AS DECIMAL(60,18))/(a.n+b.n-x.n),6) jaccard FROM pairs x JOIN sizes a ON pa=a.ProductID JOIN sizes b ON pb=b.ProductID ORDER BY pa,pb

entries.question: For every unordered pair of distinct transacted products sharing a customer, compute customer-set Jaccard similarity. WITH edges AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID, ProductID
  FROM birdbench.transactions_1k
  WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND ProductID IS NOT NULL

sizes AS (
  SELECT ProductID, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM edges
  GROUP BY ProductID
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.ProductID AS pa, b.ProductID AS pb, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM edges a
  JOIN edges b ON a.CustomerID = b.CustomerID AND a.ProductID < b.ProductID
  GROUP BY a.ProductID, b.ProductID

  x.pa AS product_a,
  x.pb AS product_b,
  x.n AS shared_customers,
  a.n + b.n - x.n AS union_customers,
  ROUND(CAST(x.n AS DECIMAL(38,6)) / (a.n + b.n - x.n), 4) AS jaccard
FROM pairs x
JOIN sizes a ON x.pa = a.ProductID
JOIN sizes b ON x.pb = b.ProductID

entries.question: For each customer currency with known transaction Price, compute median Price and median absolute deviation from that median. Return columns: currency, observation_count, median_price, mad_price. Order: currency ascending. Join customers; exclude NULL currency/Price. Normalize Price before sorting. An even sample median averages the two middle values; MAD is the same median rule on absolute deviations.

WITH norm AS (
  SELECT c.Currency AS currency,
         CASE WHEN c.Currency = 'CZK' THEN t.Price / 25.0 ELSE t.Price END AS norm_price
  FROM transactions_1k t
  JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
  WHERE t.Price IS NOT NULL AND c.Currency IS NOT NULL
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT currency, norm_price,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY currency ORDER BY norm_price) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY currency) AS cnt
  FROM norm
),
medians AS (
  SELECT currency,
         MAX(cnt) AS observation_count,
         AVG(norm_price) AS median_price
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn IN (FLOOR((cnt + 1) / 2), CEIL((cnt + 1) / 2))
  GROUP BY currency
),
devs AS (
  SELECT r.currency, ABS(r.norm_price - m.median_price) AS dev
  FROM ranked r
  JOIN medians m ON r.currency = m.currency
),
dev_ranked AS (
  SELECT currency, dev,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY currency ORDER BY dev) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY currency) AS cnt
  FROM devs
)
SELECT d.currency,
       m.observation_count,
       m.median_price,
       AVG(d.dev) AS mad_price

entries.question: Compute equal-segment standardized mean transaction Price by currency on segments present in every observed currency. Return columns: currency, common_segments, standardized_mean, raw_matched_mean. Order: currency ascending. Eligible joined rows have known currency/segment/Price. Common segments occur in every currency in that eligible universe. Standardized mean equally weights segment mean Prices; raw matched mean weights all eligible rows in the common segments.
entries.sql:
WITH eligible AS (
    SELECT t.Price, c.Currency, c.Segment
    FROM transactions_1k t
    JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    WHERE c.Currency IS NOT NULL
      AND c.Segment IS NOT NULL
      AND t.Price IS NOT NULL
),
total_currency_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Currency) AS cnt FROM eligible
),
segment_currency_count AS (
    SELECT Segment, COUNT(DISTINCT Currency) AS cnt
    FROM eligible
    GROUP BY Segment
),
common_segments AS (
    SELECT scc.Segment
    FROM segment_currency_count scc
    CROSS JOIN total_currency_count tcc
    WHERE scc.cnt = tcc.cnt
),
seg_means AS (
    SELECT e.Currency, e.Segment, AVG(e.Price) AS seg_mean
    FROM eligible e
    INNER JOIN common_segments cs ON e.Segment = cs.Segment
    GROUP BY e.Currency, e.Segment
),
standardized AS (
    SELECT Currency, AVG(seg_mean) AS standardized_mean
    FROM seg_means
    GROUP BY Currency
),
raw AS (
    SELECT e.Currency, AVG(e.Price) AS raw_matched_mean
    FROM eligible e
    INNER JOIN common_segments cs ON e.Segment = cs.Segment
    GROUP BY e.Currency
),
common_segments_str AS (
    SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(Segment ORDER BY Segment SEPARATOR ',') AS common_segments
    FROM common_segments
)
SELECT
    cur.Currency AS currency,
    css.common_segments AS common_segments,
    s.standardized_mean AS standardized_mean,
    r.raw_matched_mean AS raw_matched_mean
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT Currency FROM eligible) cur
CROSS JOIN common_segments_str css
LEFT JOIN standardized s ON cur.Currency = s.Currency
LEFT JOIN raw r ON cur.Currency = r.Currency
ORDER BY cur.Currency ASC;
